lens: The evidence pool lacks explicitly tagged fact IDs, preventing binding of specific citations for a publishable thesis, indicating the data is too narrow or noisy for direct synthesis. This framing highlights the need for curated fact extraction before systematic reviews can proceed.
known_to_ignore: Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets and osteomalacia
Vitamin D levels correlate with bone turnover and osteoporosis risk
tensions: Hint 16 (paper=10.1093/gerona/glad073) shows no improvement in bone density with supplementation vs. Hint 5 (paper=10.1210/er.2018-00126) linking deficiency to accelerated bone loss

Hint 2 (paper=10.1002/14651858.cd011564.pub3) reports high uncertainty in vitamin D's effect on all-cause mortality vs. hints 4 and 13 (papers 10.3389/fpubh.2020.00513 and 10.3390/nu13030717) suggesting associations with COVID-19 mortality
gaps: Obese individuals (hint 1, paper=10.1002/jbmr.3884) with reduced CYP2R1 mRNA and its impact on vitamin D metabolism
Elderly COVID-19 patients with severe vitamin D deficiency (median 3.0 ng/mL in deaths, hint 13) and intervention studies
Cancer patients on immunotherapy (hints 20-24, paper=10.1001/jama.2019.2402) exploring vitamin D's role in progression-free survival
reviewer_objections: Insufficient direct evidence from randomized trials to link vitamin D supplementation to extended healthspan outcomes
Reliance on observational data for COVID-19 associations introduces confounding biases
Heterogeneity in dose regimes (200-2000 IU/day) and population baselines complicates meta-analysis
next_extractions: Extract studies on CYP2R1 enzyme activity in obesity and vitamin D bioavailability
Harvest clinical trial data on vitamin D doses (e.g., 800-2000 IU/day) in institutionalized elderly for mortality endpoints
Identify datasets on vitamin D and PaO2/FiO2 ratios in COVID-19 respiratory distress
Gather longitudinal studies on vitamin D supplementation in cancer immunotherapy with PFS or OS outcomes
